name: CVE-2026-105437
description: PoC for CVE-2026-105437 — Git's three-way merge (xdiff/xmerge.c) sizes the merge output buffer in a 32-bit int, so a committed conflict-marker-size gitattribute plus many conflicts overflows it and the merge is written past an undersized heap allocation; git merge-tree is the primary vector. Validated on 2.56.0 (SIGSEGV) vs 2.56.1.
vuln_description:
Affected versions of Git have a heap buffer overflow in the three-way merge
code (xdiff), which an attacker can trigger through a repository they
control.

When Git merges a file, it first adds up the size of the merged
output, allocates a buffer of that size, and then writes the output into
it. That total was kept in a 32-bit signed integer. The
conflict-marker-size attribute, which can be set from a committed
.gitattributes file, accepts any positive integer, and the markers are
written several times for every conflict. A small file with a huge marker
size and many separate conflicts can therefore push the total past 4 GiB,
so the integer wraps to a small value and Git writes attacker-controlled
merge output past the end of a buffer that is too small. At minimum this
crashes Git, and because the overflow is large and its contents are largely
attacker-controlled, worse heap corruption is possible.

Any command that does a textual three-way merge can trigger it, such
as git-merge(1), git-rebase(1), git-cherry

EpsImagePlugin.Ghostscript passes a caller-controlled input filename after -f without converting it to a safe absolute path, so a name beginning with a hyphen can be interpreted as a Ghostscript option. An attacker who controls the filename can inject Ghostscript arguments. Arbitrary command execution specifically requires a leading @ argument-file filename and control of the referenced text file containing additional Ghostscript arguments; the reported chain reproduces with the default -dSAFER invocation. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.
